mission: Common area reconfigured as tactical briefing. Per D6 Fix 1, the intellectual naming of what Veraine has been doing lands here in response-quadrant processing — Ben's body knew it at Kolven (R08a, cascade-acceleration seed), and now the group names it: Veraine is not studying, she is engineering. The array-dependency fact (from Ben's and Desh's converged read at Ch 13) forces a specific route-restructure: skip ahead of Veraine rather than follow. Ben lays out the intercept. His mother's cadence in his voice without him meaning it. Sera straightens her spine and shifts from adversarial to subordinate. 'Tell me where to stand, Skywalker.' The last person she chose to follow sealed her in a wall. Per B1, Ben is now holding the array-dependency fact at scene one; it reroutes the mission. Per the first Luke-pressure blank-template beat: Ben drafts a new partial report to Luke, cannot finish the template that requires the mission-state field, leaves it open on his datapad on the briefing table where Desh sees it. The missed check-in from Ch 13 has become a missed-report pattern.
why_now: Post-midpoint. Part 3 opens. Ben's body-knowledge from the breach needs to arrive in the room as language so the group can operate on it. The array-dependency is the decision-forcing fact that reroutes every chapter from here to Ch 20. Sera has to offer him something she does not yet realise she is offering in the pattern of how she offers it — and Ben has to receive it while the blank Luke template sits unfilled on the table.
conflict: Ben takes the room by assembling the facts, not by asserting rank. Naming Veraine as engineer rather than student means committing to an intercept route and accepting that the institutional chain-of-command he would normally loop in is now, specifically, not looped in. Sera accepts his authority conditionally. That is also the sentence she said a thousand years ago to the last commander she trusted, and she cannot yet see the rhyme. On Ben's datapad, the report template sits with its mission-state field blank — every sentence he tries to put in it would be a version of the conversation he just had, and none of the versions are complete.
turning_point: Sera shifts from adversarial to subordinate and calls Ben 'Skywalker' with something new inside the word — investment, not warmth. The gift is also the test. Meanwhile, the Luke report template sits open on the briefing table with the mission-state field empty; Desh sees it, Ben sees Desh see it, neither speaks.
opening_hook: Ben stands in the center of the common area and lays out the plan — Veraine as engineer, not student; the array-dependency at Veranthos; the intercept route. His mother's voice in his cadence without him meaning it to be
closing_hook: Sera calls him 'Skywalker' with something that wasn't there before. Not warmth — investment. She has chosen to follow him. The last person she chose to follow sealed her in a wall. The Luke report template is still open on the briefing table with the mission-state field blank
emotional_trajectory: Assumed authority -> the intellectual naming landing in the room -> the test of command -> the burden of earned trust -> the unfilled template

stakes.external: The strategy to intercept Veraine must work or they lose the race; the array-dependency fact makes Veranthos the specific destination that determines the endgame shape

notes: Per D6 Fix 1, the intellectual naming of Veraine's engineering lands in this scene — deferred from Ch 13 midpoint per the restructure. The naming is in Ben's voice, delivered through the briefing, not through narrator exposition. Ben names it because his body has known it since Kolven; the naming is the response-quadrant processing, not a new discovery. Per B1, Ben already holds the array-dependency fact at scene one — it is the premise of the intercept, not the conclusion of a debate. Per R11, Ben's close-third still tracks what he has earned; his analytical register has sharpened at the Ch 13 midpoint and is permitted to be sharper here than in earlier chapters. Not late-Ben register yet — mid-Ben, transitional. Sera's gift of 'Tell me where to stand, Skywalker' is the Gavran pattern in miniature — she does not see the repetition yet and the book does not yet let her. The reader feels the weight because the line mirrors her ghost. Per R11 and per the Ch 19 recognition placement, Ben does not narrate that Sera is repeating her past. He feels the weight of the sentence without placing it; the placement is the Ch 19 recognition. Per D7 Component B, the narrator does not over-signal Torin's direction past Ben's perception; Torin's nod in this scene reads to Ben as approval, and the narrator does not correct for it. The blank Luke report template is the first visible Luke-pressure beat after the Ch 13 unmade call — the withholding is becoming a pattern with specific artefacts (blank template, unfilled field). Per the extended_metadata.jacen_parallel touchpoint and PP26 (the unmade Luke call promise), this beat reinforces the promise without naming it. Per D3, the Weave terminology holds — array-dependency, Weave-architecture, etc. Voice: Zahn-procedural for the briefing spine, with Bujold-interior permitted in the moments around Ben's awareness of the template on the table (self-aware without self-pity, the sentence he cannot finish and the one he gives Sera instead). Anti-patterns: (a) Ben does not explicitly notice his mother's cadence in his own voice — the reader hears Mara through the rhythm of the sentences, not through a line of interiority; (b) Ben does not articulate the Sera/Gavran echo; (c) no character comments aloud on the blank report template — it is an artefact in the room. Primary anchor: Zahn (briefing procedural); supporting anchor: Bujold (Ben's interior register of the unfilled template), Allston (five-voice ensemble distinction).
